subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw expose inter-session run progress through a new `sessions_subscribe` or `agent.events` API, a `sessions_send` progress option, or a narrower channel-specific bridge?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the API shape, authorization model, redaction policy, event buffering, retention, replay, and Telegram/channel delivery behavior are product and security decisions rather than a deterministic fix.

options.title: Design a gateway run-event API
options.body: Add a bounded, authorized, redacted event read or subscription surface that `sessions_send` and clients can share for long-running runs.

options.title: Keep final-only semantics
options.body: Treat `sessions_send` as accepted/final-only, document the behavior, and leave polling/history as the supported progress workaround.

options.title: Use channel-specific bridges
options.body: Forward a narrow set of progress updates to selected channels such as Telegram without creating a general gateway event API.

recommendation.title: Design a gateway run-event API
recommendation.body: Add a bounded, authorized, redacted event read or subscription surface that `sessions_send` and clients can share for long-running runs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history places the most direct `sessions_send`, A2A, and ACP A2A work in this area with `vincentkoc`.
